company: Regal Partners Global Investments Limited (formerly VGI Partners Global Investments Limited)
title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Relevant Persons
tiers.description: Any director or company secretary of any Group member; anyone with authority and responsibility for planning, direction and control of the Company's activities (KMP); employees and personnel of the Investment Manager (Regal Partners Limited) and its subsidiaries, or anyone else providing services to it, including contractors/consultants whose engagement incorporates this policy; and any other person the Board designates.

tiers.name: Directors and Company Secretary
tiers.description: Directors and the Company Secretary of the Company (excluding the Chair); distinguished only for the identity of the Clearance Officer, which is the Chair of the Board.

tiers.name: Chair of the Board
tiers.description: The Chair; distinguished only for the identity of the Clearance Officer, which is the Chair of the Board's Audit and Risk Committee.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A family member (including a child), a nominee (including an investment manager managing funds on the Relevant Person's behalf), a trust of which the Relevant Person, a family member, or a family-controlled company is trustee or beneficiary, a partner, or a company the Relevant Person controls. Uses the Clearance Officer of their Principal.

definitions.hedging_definition: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Company Securities; put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.

windows.start_anchor: 5 business days before the scheduled release of half-year or full-year results, or before announcement of a dividend or capital management initiative that may have a material price impact
windows.end_anchor: commencement of trading on the first trading day after that release or announcement

windows.start_anchor: commencement of on-market share purchases under the 'performance fee reinvestment mechanism'
commencement of on-market share purchases under the Company's dividend reinvestment plan

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may determine any other blackout period from time to time (clause 9.3(d)); the Policy does not state that such a determination itself is confidential, though a Clearance Officer's refusal of Clearance must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on using Derivatives (defined to include put/call options, forwards, swaps, CFDs, caps and collars) over unvested Company Securities, to prevent value being realised ahead of vesting.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company Securities.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Company Securities are expressly permitted, subject to the balance of the Policy (i.e. prior Clearance, outside blackout periods, not while holding Inside Information).
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: 'Caps and collars' and 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' are named within the Derivatives definition; hedging of unvested securities is therefore banned via the Derivatives prohibition.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company Securities.

rules.detail: A hedging arrangement (cap, collar, swap etc.) over vested securities is a Derivative and is permitted subject to Clearance and the balance of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: A prepaid forward or similar monetisation is a 'forward contract' Derivative and is banned outright over unvested securities.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company Securities.

rules.detail: Forward-contract style monetisation over vested securities is a Derivative permitted subject to Clearance and the balance of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Short selling (borrowing and selling shares) is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.
Contracts for difference are named within the Derivatives definition and are banned over unvested Company Securities.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company Securities.

rules.detail: CFDs over vested Company Securities are permitted as a Derivative subject to Clearance and the balance of the Policy.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company Securities, provided any Dealing complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Default prohibition on margin loans (and other margin lending arrangements) to fund acquisition of Company Securities, but with an express carve-out where the Board expressly permits it.
rules.evidence: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.

rules.detail: Using Company Securities as security against loan repayments is prohibited by default, save where the Board expressly permits it.
rules.evidence: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from ... [entering into arrangements] in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.

rules.detail: The prohibition is confined to margin loans and 'other types of margin lending arrangements'; it does not purport to reach every conceivable secured financing structure, but a bank loan secured on the collared shares falls within it and needs Board permission.
rules.evidence: Margin loans to support an investment in Company Securities (and other types of margin lending arrangements) can compromise compliance with this policy, as the loan's terms may compel the sale of Company Securities during a blackout period or when the Relevant Person has relevant Inside Information.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on short-term Dealing, defined as within a 3 month period, and on frequent/regular trading activity.
rules.evidence: A Relevant Person or Associate must not engage in short term Dealing in Company Securities. Short-term trading includes Dealing in securities within a 3 month period and entering into other short-term dealings in a manner which involves frequent and regular trading activity.

clearance.evidence: A Clearance ... will remain in force for the date of approval only, unless otherwise notified by the Clearance Officer ... can be given or refused by the Clearance Officer in its absolute discretion without providing any reasons; and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.
Clearance Officer means: ... for the Company Secretary or a director of the Company (excluding the Chair of the Board), the Chair of the Board

clearance.approver: Chair of the Board's Audit and Risk Committee
clearance.evidence: Clearance Officer means: ... for the Chair of the Board, the Chair of the Board's Audit and Risk Committee

short_term.evidence: Short-term trading includes Dealing in securities within a 3 month period and entering into other short-term dealings in a manner which involves frequent and regular trading activity.

exceptions.evidence: if a person has a pressing financial commitment that cannot otherwise be satisfied and all reasonable alternatives have been investigated

if a person is required by court order, or enforceable undertaking (eg in a bona fide family settlement) to transfer or sell Company Securities or there is another overriding legal requirement to do so

undertake a Dealing in units of or interests in, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme investing primarily in Company Securities) whereby the assets of that fund or scheme are invested at a third party's sole discretion

Deal in Company Securities under an offer or invitation made by the Company to all or most of its ordinary shareholders – such as an offer or invitation under a rights issue, bonus issue, equal access buy-back or in lieu of a cash dividend

undertake to accept, or accept, an offer for Company Securities made under a takeover bid or dispose of Company Securities under a court-approved compromise or arrangement under Part 5.1 of the Corporations Act

exercise (but not sell Company Securities following exercise) an option or right under an equity incentive plan, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for exercise or conversion falls during a blackout period ... provided that the Clearance Officer has confirmed that the exercise is permitted

an off-market transaction involving the transfer or other disposal of Company Securities between a Relevant Person or Associate and any of the following: an Associate of the Relevant Person ... a company, trust or other entity over which the Relevant Person or Associate ... has control or significant influence ... or a superannuation fund or other pension or saving scheme in which the Relevant Person or an Associate ... is a beneficiary
undertake a Dealing which involves or results in the forfeiture, lapse, cancellation or surrender of Company Securities under an equity incentive plan

external_documents: Management Agreement between the Company and Regal Partners Limited dated 19 July 2017
exemption_authority: The Board may expressly permit an otherwise-prohibited margin loan or share-secured funding arrangement (clause 17.2). Separately, the Clearance Officer has absolute discretion to grant Clearance to deal during a blackout period in exceptional circumstances -- a court order/enforceable undertaking, or a pressing financial commitment with no reasonable alternative (clause 11.2) -- given in writing, not retrospective, and lapsing immediately if the applicant acquires Inside Information. Non-administrative amendments to the Policy require Board approval, and amendments to blackout periods, exclusions or exceptional-circumstances provisions must be released to ASX (clause 22).

bespoke_clauses.topic: margin loan / share-secured loan ban with Board carve-out
bespoke_clauses.clause: Save where expressly permitted by the Board, Relevant Persons are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements to fund the acquisition of Company Securities or in relation to which Company Securities may be used as security against loan repayments.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank loan secured on the collared shares is a margin lending arrangement caught by clause 17 and is prohibited by default; it can only proceed with the Board's express, discretionary permission.

bespoke_clauses.topic: caps and collars named as Derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives ... includes ... put or call options, forward contracts ... swaps, contracts for difference ... caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An equity collar (put and call) is squarely and by name a Derivative under this Policy, governed by clause 16: banned over unvested securities but permitted over vested securities subject to Clearance.

bespoke_clauses.clause: A Clearance ... will remain in force for the date of approval only, unless otherwise notified by the Clearance Officer (if the Dealing is not placed within this time, the Clearance will no longer have effect and a new Clearance must be requested and obtained)
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Execution of a cleared collar with the bank must occur on the day Clearance is given, or a fresh Clearance request is needed, requiring tight coordination between the Relevant Person, the bank and the Clearance Officer.

bespoke_clauses.clause: What will the public perception be if it were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a cleared, vested-share collar could be refused Clearance, or criticised after the fact, if it would fail this broad reputational test, adding a discretionary filter beyond the black-letter rules.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If a Relevant Person may not Deal in Company Securities, he or she must also prevent such Dealing by his or her Associate.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar or secured loan cannot be routed through a spouse, family trust or controlled company to escape the derivatives or margin-lending restrictions, since the Relevant Person must actively prevent the Associate from dealing.

summary: A funded OTC equity collar over vested shares is achievable for a Relevant Person of Regal Partners Global Investments Limited (formerly VGI Partners Global Investments Limited), but on conditions. The Policy expressly defines 'caps and collars' as Derivatives, banned outright over unvested Company Securities (clause 16.2) but permitted over vested Company Securities provided the Dealing otherwise complies with the Policy (clause 16.3) -- i.e. prior Clearance from the Clearance Officer, outside blackout periods (or under a hardship or court-order exception), and not while holding Inside Information. The loan leg is more constrained: clause 17 prohibits margin loans or similar funding arrangements to acquire Company Securities, or using Company Securities as security for loan repayments, 'save where expressly permitted by the Board', so a bank loan secured on the collared shares needs specific Board approval rather than being available as of right. Clearance obtained is valid only on the day it is given, lapses immediately if Inside Information is later acquired, and Associates (spouse, family trust, controlled company) are equally bound, so the structure cannot be routed around a Relevant Person via family arrangements. Overall verdict: permitted with prior Clearance for the derivative legs over vested shares, but the secured loan requires the Board's express, discretionary permission.
